title: Dependency Security and Reproducible Builds
learning_outcomes: Explain what dependency security and reproducible builds contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: auditing dependencies.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Composer describes dependencies and maps namespaces to source files. Lockfiles make application installs reproducible; declared constraints and maintenance/security review keep dependency choices intentional. In this lesson, focus on auditing dependencies; then compare it with removing unused packages. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use dependency security and reproducible builds when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Composer describes dependencies and maps namespaces to source files. Lockfiles make application installs reproducible; declared constraints and maintenance/security review keep dependency choices intentional. For dependency security and reproducible builds, begin with auditing dependencies. Also distinguish removing unused packages; lockfile review; build consistency. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.why: Updates can overwrite manual changes and make builds irreproducible.
common_mistakes.fix: Declare dependencies in composer.json and regenerate the lock/autoload state using Composer.

common_mistakes.why: Different environments may resolve different dependency versions.
common_mistakes.fix: Commit the lockfile for applications and use the project’s intended install workflow.

common_mistakes.problem: Choosing a package by download count alone.
common_mistakes.why: Popularity does not prove security, maintenance, or version compatibility.
common_mistakes.fix: Review maintenance activity, releases, dependencies, license, and docs.
